edits.find: Dried beans: About $1.50 a pound and around 15 cents per half-cup cooked serving.
edits.replace: Dried beans: Among the cheapest protein in the store, and one bag cooks up into a lot of half-cup servings.

edits.find: Lentils: Roughly $1.80 a pound, cook in 20 minutes with no soaking, and land near 18 cents a serving.
edits.replace: Lentils: Run {{live-unit:brown-lentils:lb}} a pound dry, cook in 20 minutes with no soaking, and stretch into a lot of servings.
edits.why: brown-lentils is the board's lentils commodity (its match takes plain lentils); the per-serving cents came from the typed pound price and go.

edits.find: Eggs: Even at $3.50 a dozen, that is under 30 cents each for complete protein you can cook a dozen ways.

edits.find: Canned tuna: About $1 a can for roughly 20 grams of protein.
edits.replace: Canned tuna: Runs {{live-unit:canned-tuna:oz}} an ounce, and a can gives you roughly 20 grams of protein.
edits.why: canned-tuna is priced per ounce; a can is not an allowed per, so the price moves to the ounce and the can keeps its protein claim.

edits.why: peanut-butter is a board commodity; the jar price becomes a per-pound price and the derived per-serving cents go.
